$comment: nodes=modules, edges=[cause,effect] where cause is imported-by effect. Nodes are SEEDED from the chosen architecture (CMIS system design v1 §6) because the repo has no code yet; re-run tools/graphizer.mjs --write once modules exist and keep the invariants block below.

read_path_fails_open.rule: GET /v1/memories:retrieve never returns 5xx. On any internal failure it returns HTTP 200 with {"memories": [], "degraded": true}.
read_path_fails_open.why: System design invariant #1 — memory retrieval is optional; the primary response path must work with zero memories returned.

read_path_makes_no_external_calls.rule: Nothing reachable from app/api/routes_retrieve may import worker/llm_providers or call an external network endpoint. Embeddings, keyword and graph signals are local only.
read_path_makes_no_external_calls.why: Keeps the <150ms p95 read budget and removes external-provider risk from the user-facing path (ADR 0003, §13).

no_durable_write_without_provenance_and_.rule: Every row in the memories table has non-null source_turn_ids, actor, created_at and a pii_verdict_id; no candidate text is sent to worker/llm_providers before worker/pii_filter has returned a verdict.
no_durable_write_without_provenance_and_.why: System design invariants #2 and #3 plus threat model §4 — PII filter is pre-send, not just pre-store, and no fact is anonymous.

tenant_isolation_is_db_enforced.rule: Every table holding memory content or audit rows has RLS enabled with a tenant_id policy; a query that omits the tenant filter still returns zero cross-tenant rows.
tenant_isolation_is_db_enforced.why: ADR 0006 — cross-tenant leakage is the highest-severity trust failure and application-layer scoping has no backstop.

background_jobs_never_block_the_request_.rule: app/api/** must not import worker/write_gate, worker/decay_job or worker/reflection_agent; admission is reachable only via worker/queue, and every outbound call in worker/** has an explicit timeout.
background_jobs_never_block_the_request_.why: System design invariant #6 + ADR 0003 — the Write Gate is async and queue-backed; latency and rate limits stay off the user-facing path.
